title: Application API reference
description: Reference Gonex construction, module registration, typed routing, lifecycle and resource APIs.
text:
These decisions began as the phase 0 contract and now describe the implemented application API. Historical results remain in the phase reports(/docs/main/implementation-record).


 Module and toolchain

The Go module is github.com/amkargar/gonex; the product name is goNex. The repository baseline is Go 1.27.1. Exact dependency versions are pinned in go.mod(https://github.com/amkargar/gonex/blob/main/go.mod). See release policy(/docs/main/release/) for configured and verified platforms.

 Construction and registration

- gonex.New(config.Config) (app.App, error) validates settings without binding ports.
- Module.Register(Registrar) error declares a module's routes and resources.
- App.Register(...Module) error registers explicitly in argument order, atomically per call.
- Registration freezes at startup. A failed registration call leaves the application unchanged.
- Registrar.Handle(method, path string, handlers ...gin.HandlerFunc) error is a raw Gin escape hatch. Use typed HTTP registration for public contracts.

 Routing and contracts

Route identity is the uppercase method plus full path. Duplicate and incompatible wildcard routes fail before serving. Runtime health/readiness and enabled document paths reject conflicting registrations.

http.Register builds a typed endpoint contract. Request origins, supported validation constraints and schema projection are checked together. Contracts detach mutable metadata at registration. Raw Gin routes are not included in OpenAPI.

HTTP versions are explicit adapter packages. gRPC remains optional, with versioned Protobuf packages and independently managed servers/clients. See HTTP contracts(/docs/main/http/) and gRPC(/docs/main/grpc/).

 Resource ownership

Registrar.Manage(Resource) error owns resources implementing Start(context.Context) error and Close(context.Context) error. Registration order determines startup order; close runs in reverse. Dependencies register before their consumers. An optional Errors channel reports asynchronous failure to App.Run.

Registrar.Check(name, func(context.Context) error) adds a named dependency readiness check. Resources may also implement Ready(context.Context) error. Application callbacks must honor context cancellation.

 Lifecycle guarantees

| API | Behavior |
|---|---|
| App.Start(ctx) | Starts managed resources and binds the HTTP listener synchronously |
| App.Run(ctx) | Starts, waits for cancellation/failure and shuts down within the configured budget |
| App.Shutdown(ctx) | Drains HTTP and closes resources; repeated calls are safe |
| App.Ready(ctx) | Checks running state and registered dependency readiness |

States are created, registered, starting, running, stopping and stopped. A stopped instance cannot restart. Configuration includes address, middleware, exposure switches and read/write/idle/shutdown timeouts. Zero durations use defaults; negative values fail. See modules(/docs/main/modules/) and operations(/docs/main/operations/).

title: Architecture
description: Understand Gonex package boundaries, plain Go business services and HTTP, GORM and gRPC adapters.
text:
goNex uses explicit registration and ordinary Go composition. Its business core is independent of HTTP, RPC and persistence adapters.


 Dependency direction

Business services live in modules/NAME/service.go and use plain Go values plus small interfaces owned by the consumer. HTTP adapters own schemas and request mapping; GORM repositories and gRPC clients implement business interfaces at their boundaries. Services should not import Gin, GORM, gRPC, Protobuf or transport DTOs.

mermaid
flowchart LR
    HTTPHTTP adapter --> ServiceBusiness service
    RPCgRPC server adapter --> Service
    Service --> PortLocal dependency interface
    DatabaseGORM repository -. implements .-> Port
    ClientgRPC client adapter -. implements .-> Port


 Registration and lifecycle

A module receives registration capabilities, never ownership of a listener. Registration is explicit, ordered and atomic per App.Register call. The application owns listeners and managed resources. Startup failures close started resources; shutdown drains HTTP and closes resources in reverse order. Stopped applications cannot restart.

Dependencies register before consumers. Context-aware resource lifecycles make background work and cleanup explicit. See modules and lifecycle(/docs/main/modules/).

 HTTP and RPC boundaries

HTTP is unversioned by default. OpenAPI projects the registered typed endpoints. Independent versioned HTTP adapters can share one core service; legacy routes remain unless replacement is explicit.

gRPC is opt-in and has no default listener. Protobuf packages and Go paths carry their API major. Contracts use a separate Go module so services can depend on a shared wire contract without importing each other's business code.

 Generator ownership

Generators own marked registries and record hashes in .gonex.json. They plan and validate writes first, reject handwritten destination collisions and support dry runs. Runtime composition does not scan source or depend on a dependency-injection container.

Independent services have their own Go modules, configuration and migrations. A local go.work file is a development convenience; production dependencies must resolve independently.

 Dependencies

The framework is not dependency-free. The root go.mod declares 10 direct dependencies; indirect dependencies are recorded separately in go.mod and go.sum. Optional integrations share the module dependency graph, but HTTP-only applications need not import or start database/RPC adapters.

| Direct dependency | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| github.com/gin-gonic/gin | HTTP routing and middleware |
| github.com/go-playground/validator/v10 | Typed input validation |
| github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 | Offline OpenAPI schema validation |
| github.com/ncruces/go-sqlite3/gormlite | CGO-free SQLite integration |
| gorm.io/driver/postgres | PostgreSQL driver |
| gorm.io/gorm | Optional persistence adapter |
| google.golang.org/grpc | Optional RPC transport |
| google.golang.org/protobuf | Protobuf runtime and generation support |
| github.com/bufbuild/protocompile | Contract compilation tooling |
| golang.org/x/mod | Go module validation and generator edits |

The list above groups responsibilities; the actual source of truth is go.mod(https://github.com/amkargar/gonex/blob/main/go.mod), including any separate module requirements. Check its first require block when updating the dependency badge.

 Design decisions and limits

Prefer small consumer-owned interfaces and explicit constructors over global registries. Keep validation and the exported contract coherent, rather than silently projecting unsupported DTO behavior. Keep migrations explicit and immutable.

Service discovery is static, cancellation is cooperative and generators do not invent business mappings. See API decisions(/docs/main/api-reference/), upgrade policy(/docs/main/upgrades/) and release scope(/docs/main/release/).

title: CLI reference
description: Reference Gonex commands for safe project scaffolding, modules, API versions, gRPC generation and database migrations.
text:
The executable is named gonex; framework branding is goNex. Run commands from the generated project or workspace root. Positional names come before flags.


 Project creation

sh
gonex new NAME --module IMPORT_PATH --framework-version VERSION --arch monolith|microservices --dry-run


The architecture defaults to monolith; the framework version defaults to v0.1.0. The destination must not exist. Use a resolvable release version or the explicit local checkout override(/docs/main/quick-start/use-an-unpublished-checkout).

 Modules and services

sh
gonex create module NAME --transport http|none|grpc|http,grpc --http-version vN --db --service NAME --dry-run
gonex create service NAME --dry-run
gonex create client PROVIDER --service CONSUMER --module MODULE --version v1 --dry-run


| Option | Behavior |
|---|---|
| --transport | Defaults to http; none creates only the business core |
| --http-version | Starts an HTTP module directly in a version package, without legacy routes |
| --db | Adds a store interface, GORM adapter, model and explicit migration |
| --service | Selects the owning service in a microservices workspace |
| --version | Selects the provider's Protobuf API major for a client skeleton |
| --dry-run | Validates and prints the proposed plan without changing project files |

create service requires a microservices workspace. A client skeleton uses real generated service constructors but leaves domain mapping and injection to the developer. Run go mod tidy in each affected module after adding dependencies.

 Adapter changes

sh
gonex module version NAME --http vN --policy preserve|replace --prefix PATH --service NAME --dry-run
gonex module enable NAME --grpc --service NAME --dry-run


Versioning defaults to preserve and /api/vN. replace stops registering legacy routes while retaining their source. Existing version packages are not overwritten. Enabling gRPC preserves handwritten source and requires the supported injectable service factory. See HTTP versions(/docs/main/versioning/) and microservices(/docs/main/microservices/).

 Run and verify

sh
gonex run --service NAME
gonex build --service NAME
gonex check --service NAME
gonex --help
gonex --version


run invokes the Go executable path for the project. build builds its packages; check runs tests, vet and build. Child command failures preserve their exit codes. A workspace command must identify a service when selection is ambiguous.

 OpenAPI

sh
gonex openapi generate --out openapi.json --http-version vN --service NAME --dry-run
gonex openapi validate --file openapi.json --against BASELINE --service NAME


Generation executes the project's initialization/export path without starting listeners, validates the result and writes the output. It exports the legacy document unless --http-version selects a registered major. Validation is offline; --against additionally runs conservative compatibility checks against a baseline. A generation dry run does not execute project code.

 Database migrations

sh
gonex db migrate --service NAME --dry-run
gonex db status --service NAME --dry-run


Configure DATABASE_URL and, where needed, DATABASE_DIALECT in the executable's environment. Migrations are explicit; serving does not automatically change schemas. Dry runs do not connect to the database. See database behavior(/docs/main/database/).

 Protobuf contracts

sh
gonex grpc generate --dry-run
gonex grpc check


Run from a supported project/workspace, service or contracts root. Generation compiles and checks contracts, then invokes pinned official plugins and stages the resulting files. Dry runs omit plugins and writes. check compares descriptors to the stored baseline. Neither command substitutes for the release workflow's Buf gate; see gRPC contracts(/docs/main/grpc/).

 Generator safety

Generators plan and validate paths and collisions before writes. They reject traversal, symlinks and handwritten-file overwrites, hash-check tool-owned registries and support dry runs. .gonex.json records ownership metadata; do not delete it to bypass a conflict.

New projects use a staged rename. Existing projects use an exclusive lock, staging and rollback on ordinary application errors; multi-file updates are not power-loss atomic. After an interrupted process, inspect .gonex.lock and proposed changes before recovering. See getting started(/docs/main/quick-start/generator-safety).

title: Databases and migrations
description: Use optional GORM adapters with SQLite or PostgreSQL and explicit, checksum-verified SQL migrations.
text:
Configure a database resource

orm.New(orm.OptionsDialect:"sqlite", DSNEnv:"DATABASE_URL") constructs a resource without pinging. Register it with Registrar.Manage; startup opens/pings and shutdown closes its SQL pool. orm.Open(ctx, options) opens immediately for explicit tools/tests. Never log DSNs. Driver errors from opening/pinging are redacted. Pool limits, idle time and lifetime are configurable. The initial verified dialect is real file-backed SQLite using ncruces/gormlite (CGO-free); PostgreSQL uses GORM's official driver.

 Keep repositories at the boundary

Services define local repository interfaces; GORM adapters map values and not-found/unique errors. orm.Transaction accepts a GORM callback only at the adapter boundary. A service needing atomic multi-write behavior should define a small local transaction callback interface implemented by that adapter.

 Apply immutable migrations

Migrations are immutable UTF-8 SQL files named 000001_description.up.sql. Use migration.New(pool, dialect, files) with an embedded or directory fs.FS, then explicitly call Up(ctx) or Status(ctx). SQL must be transaction-compatible; do not put BEGIN/COMMIT, nontransactional DDL or connection-level PRAGMAs inside a migration. The runner uses one transaction for the full pending batch, a version/checksum history table, SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE via serializable isolation, and PostgreSQL transaction advisory locks. Concurrent runners cannot apply the same migration twice. Changes to applied contents/names, missing versions and out-of-order history fail clearly. Repeating an unchanged migration set is a no-op. Status initializes an empty history table if needed.

No AutoMigrate or implicit application-start schema changes. Down migrations are deliberately absent from the example because dropping persisted users is destructive. Forward corrections use new versions.

 Run the SQLite example

PowerShell example:

powershell
$env:DATABASE_DIALECT='sqlite'
$env:DATABASE_URL='file:users.db?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)'
go run ./examples/basic migrate
go run ./examples/basic


POST /users persists rows; subsequent GET /users/id works across application restarts. Without DATABASE_URL the example uses its in-memory repository, and HTTP-only apps import no persistence package.

 Verify database behavior

go test ./... always tests file-backed SQLite CRUD, transactions, migration rollback/checksums/concurrency and lifecycle cleanup. PostgreSQL integration is explicitly skipped unless GONEX_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN identifies an empty disposable test database; it is never inferred from production DATABASE_URL. PostgreSQL credentials and deployment-specific behavior require that integration environment.

title: gRPC and contracts
description: Configure optional Gonex gRPC servers and clients, versioned Protobuf contracts, deadlines, TLS and mTLS.
text:
Opt in to gRPC

Import github.com/amkargar/gonex/grpc only in transport/bootstrap code. HTTP-only modules do not import it or start gRPC listeners. config.ConfigDisableHTTP:true permits a gRPC-only process. Manage servers and client pools with Registrar.Manage so failed startup/shutdown releases them. Resources exposing Errors() also report asynchronous failures to App.Run.

 Register a server

grpc.NewServer(ServerOptionsAddress:...,TLS:...) constructs without binding. Supply generated registration callbacks through Server.Register, then let the app Start/Close it. The built-in standard gRPC health service reports serving status. Application services must not import gRPC or generated messages; map at server/client boundaries using ToStatus/FromStatus. Unknown errors are redacted.

 Configure TLS and mTLS

TLS is required by default. Load a server certificate and trust roots using crypto/tls and crypto/x509. mTLS uses RequireAndVerifyClientCert plus ClientCAs; the client supplies its certificate. Client InsecureSkipVerify is rejected. Only explicit DevelopmentInsecure permits plaintext for local development. Keep caller-provided TLS certificate/key material immutable after configuration.

 Reuse managed clients

Create one immutable ClientConfig per target/security/transport setup with NewClientConfig. Reuse that config with a shared Clients manager to reuse a connection concurrently. Different immutable configs never share a connection, even when targets are equal; this avoids credential/identity/dialer mixing. grpc.Client(pool, config, generated.NewServiceClient) returns a typed generated client. Creation is lazy; pool.Ready(ctx,config) separately proves connectivity and requires a bounded caller context. Registry resolves explicit service names to configs. No write retry policy is installed; configured retry policies are disabled.

 Set deadlines and drain requests

Default unary and stream RPC timeouts are five seconds, configurable per server/client; shorter incoming contexts win. Stream timeouts bound the whole stream lifetime. Handlers must honor their contexts. Server.Close uses graceful stop, then force-stop if the supplied context expires. App.Run supplies its configured shutdown timeout.

 Generate versioned contracts

Contracts are a separate Go module at contracts/. All packages and Go paths are versioned. gonex grpc generate compiles with pinned Buf protocompile v0.14.1 and invokes official protoc-gen-go v1.36.10 / protoc-gen-go-grpc v1.6.0. This Go-only compiler is the one used by Buf; protoc installation is unnecessary. --dry-run compiles/checks without plugins or writes. Generated files are staged; sources and handwritten adapters are preserved. Network/cache access is needed to obtain pinned tools on first use.

 Check compatibility

schema.binpb is the generated descriptor set. baseline.binpb is the explicitly frozen initial release contract. gonex grpc check rejects removed/changed files, messages, fields, enum values and RPC signatures, allowing additions. Generation enforces this baseline too. This conservative checker may require a new major for option-only changes; CI also runs Buf FILE compatibility against the same descriptor baseline. Update baselines only during a reviewed release, never to suppress a failed compatibility gate. buf.yaml and buf.gen.yaml support a standard external Buf toolchain as well.

 Run the TLS integration fixture

integration/rpc is an isolated executable-contract test module with explicit relative local replacements for this checkout. Run go -C contracts test ./... and go -C integration/rpc test ./.... Its Identity provider and Orders consumer use generated GetUser messages over real TLS, with plain Go business interfaces. These test-only replacements are not production template dependencies.

 Recovery and observability

Unary and stream recovery returns redacted Internal errors. grpc.ServerTLS and grpc.ClientTLS load verified certificate configurations with redacted file errors. The optional observability/grpc unary interceptors propagate traceparent and collect fixed-method metrics; see operations(/docs/main/operations/). Application readiness can check managed server lifecycle and explicitly registered downstream client connectivity.

 Run Buf checks

Install the pinned official Buf binary with go run ./internal/tooling/bufinstall .tools; it verifies the downloaded release checksum. Run .tools/buf lint contracts/proto and .tools/buf breaking contracts/proto --against contracts/baseline.binpb (use buf.exe on Windows). CI runs these in addition to internal checks. The runnable Identity/Orders example(https://github.com/amkargar/gonex/blob/main/examples/microservices/README.md) includes HTTP-to-gRPC mapping and TLS configuration.

title: HTTP and OpenAPI
description: Build typed HTTP endpoints with Gin adapters, request validation and OpenAPI 3.1 contracts in Gonex.
text:
Register typed endpoints

Use http.Register(registrar, http.EndpointRequest, Response...) with named Go structs, explicit method/path, operation ID, success status and handler. Business services return plain Go values; adapters map those into transport schemas. NoBody models endpoints without a body.

 Bind and validate requests

Each request wrapper field declares exactly one origin: path:"id", query:"page", header:"X-Token" or body:"true". There may be only one body field. Parameters are scalar or pointers to scalars. Path placeholders must match field bindings. Body schemas use standard json tags and validate tags. Required, min/max, email, nested structs and slice dive validation are supported. Use pointers to distinguish absent numeric/boolean values from zero/false; required on a pointer requires presence, while required on a scalar rejects its zero value.

| Origin | Example tag | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| Path | path:"id" | Required; must match the route placeholder |
| Query | query:"page" | Scalar or pointer to a scalar |
| Header | header:"X-Token" | Scalar or pointer; duplicates are rejected |
| Body | body:"true" | One JSON body field per request wrapper |

 Handle failures and limits

Malformed JSON, missing required parameters and unsupported content types return 400. Unknown or incorrectly cased JSON fields, duplicate object keys, trailing values, duplicate query/header values and null nonnullable bodies are rejected. Validation failures return 422 with field paths and codes. Request bodies default to 1 MiB; set MaxBodyBytes per endpoint. Application errors must be declared in Errors to expose their mapped status/message; undeclared/internal errors return a redacted 500. Context deadline failures return a documented 504. 204 responses have no body.

 Describe endpoint metadata

Optional summary, description, tags, request/response examples, security requirements/schemes and middleware live on the same endpoint contract. Middleware must return documented response shapes/statuses. Low-level Registrar.Handle is an escape hatch for raw Gin routes and is not projected into OpenAPI; public application endpoints should use typed registration.

 Serve and export documents

/openapi.json is enabled by default; DisableOpenAPI removes it in production. /docs is an opt-in local document link (DocsEnabled), without externally loaded assets. Runtime-owned paths reject conflicts. The specification is built and validated once during startup, not per request. App.OpenAPI() explicitly exports without starting a listener.

 Supported DTO schemas

Schemas support named/nested/recursive structs, pointers/nullability, string-keyed maps and slices; component names include a stable package hash. Input requiredness follows validation, output requiredness follows JSON omission. Nested input objects require pointers (except time.Time) so presence has an explicit representation. A value body wrapper is already required: omit its redundant required validation tag. Anonymous embedded fields, byte slices, non-string map keys, custom JSON encodings and unsupported JSON tag options require explicit DTOs. Supported validation tags are required, omitempty, min, max, email, dive and -; unsupported or contradictory constraints fail registration. The official OpenAPI Initiative 3.1 schema is vendored with its source URL; santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema v6 validates generated documents offline.

 Freeze and compare contracts

Contracts and handler slices are detached from caller-owned metadata at registration. Security requirements must reference declared schemes. Export a version with gonex openapi generate --http-version v1 --out v1.json; compare it with a released baseline using gonex openapi validate --file v1.json --against baseline.json. Compatibility checking is conservative; see upgrade policy(/docs/main/upgrades/).

title: Introduction
description: Meet Gonex: a modular Go framework for typed HTTP APIs, explicit modules, optional persistence and gRPC.
text:
Gonex is a modular Go framework for typed HTTP APIs and explicit service boundaries. Gin handles routing; typed request and response contracts describe your API; your business services stay in plain Go.

 Start here

New to Gonex? Follow the quick start(/docs/main/quick-start/) to run the repository example. Then learn about modules(/docs/main/modules/) and HTTP contracts(/docs/main/http/).

 Development snapshot

These guides document the repository’s main branch, not a published release. The upstream project reports implementation commits for phases 0–8; hosted CI, Linux race tests and live PostgreSQL verification remain pending in its README. Review the release policy(/docs/main/release/) before choosing a production dependency.

 What is included?

- Explicit module registration, managed resources and graceful shutdown.
- Gin-backed typed HTTP handlers and OpenAPI 3.1.
- Optional GORM persistence, SQL migrations and versioned HTTP adapters.
- Optional gRPC, TLS/mTLS and independent service scaffolding.
- Safe CLI generation with dry runs and handwritten file protection.

 How to read these guides

Use the sidebar to follow the build path, use the table of contents to jump within a guide, or search with Ctrl/Cmd + K. Code samples are preserved from the upstream documentation. The version selector will include released documentation when release snapshots are added.

title: Installation
description: Install prerequisites, clone Gonex, build the CLI, and resolve an unpublished local framework checkout.
text:
Prerequisites

Use Go 1.27.1, the baseline declared in the current repository, and Git. Dependency resolution requires network access or a populated module cache. Gonex has no published release yet.

 Clone the framework

sh
git clone https://github.com/amkargar/gonex.git
cd gonex


 Build the CLI

On macOS and Linux:

sh
go build -o gonex ./cmd/gonex
./gonex --help


On Windows:

powershell
go build -o gonex.exe ./cmd/gonex
.\gonex.exe --help


Put the built executable on your PATH. Do not use @latest or assume the scaffold's default v0.1.0 has been published.

 Resolve local development projects

Generated projects need an explicit local checkout override while the release is unpublished. In your generated project, replace the example with your absolute checkout path:

sh
go mod edit -replace=github.com/amkargar/gonex=/path/to/gonex
go mod tidy


The generator does not insert machine-specific paths. Before deployment, remove that override and resolve a published version when available. Microservices have a separate contracts module that must also resolve.

 Run your first application

Continue to Quick start(/docs/main/quick-start/) for the runnable example and typed endpoint program.

title: Microservices
description: Create independent Go services and versioned shared contracts with explicit typed client boundaries.
text:
Generate a workspace

Build the CLI first. These commands require resolvable framework/contracts versions or explicit local development overrides; see unpublished checkouts(/docs/main/quick-start/use-an-unpublished-checkout). Each service resolves its own dependencies.

sh
gonex new commerce --module example.com/acme/commerce --arch microservices
cd commerce
gonex create service identity
gonex create service orders
gonex create module users --service identity --transport grpc
gonex create module orders --service orders --transport http
gonex create client identity --service orders --module orders --version v1
gonex grpc generate
go -C services/identity mod tidy
go -C services/orders mod tidy
gonex check --service identity
gonex check --service orders


 Understand module boundaries

Each service has its own go.mod, main.go, config and explicit module registry. Contracts have a separate module and versioned Go packages. go.work is only local development convenience; production requires published, resolvable framework/contracts versions. Templates contain no replace directives or absolute paths. The test harness supplies explicit isolated replacements and verifies each module with GOWORK=off.

 Select services and ports

New services get distinct default loopback HTTP/gRPC ports (8081/9091, 8082/9092, ...), with HTTP_ADDRESS/GRPC_ADDRESS overrides. gonex run/build/check --service NAME select a deployable from the workspace root; ambiguity is an error. OpenAPI, database and version commands also accept --service. Each service exports its own DATABASE_URL and owns its migrations. No generated repository reads another service's database.

 Add or enable adapters

gRPC modules expose the starter service's real Message use case as Get<Module>Message with distinct versioned request/response messages. grpc-only profiles have no HTTP adapter. http,grpc profiles share one service instance and one managed server per process. All contracts and official generated stubs are staged before any project write. Dry runs create no project files. gonex module enable users --grpc --service identity preserves handwritten module/service/HTTP files and adds the transport; old template modules need the documented NewModuleService/injectable Service factory before automatic enable is safe.

 Complete client mapping

Client generation reads the selected provider/version descriptors and uses the exact generated service constructors. The adapter file contains real typed clients plus a TODO to implement the consumer's small local business interface. It does not invent domain mappings or wire dependencies into handwritten business code. Add methods mapping plain values to/from contract messages, create the adapter with a shared managed Clients pool, and inject it into your service. See integration/rpc for a completed Identity/Orders mapping, and internal/cli/microservices_test.go for a generated-workspace mapping and executable failure test.

 Configure client targets

Generated client settings use typed Address/TLS/Timeout fields; LoadIdentityClient reads CLIENTS_IDENTITY_ADDRESS, CA, SERVER_NAME, CERT, KEY and INSECURE. Address defaults to the provider's development loopback endpoint. This is explicit static configuration, not distributed service discovery.

 Configure transport security

Production gRPC needs GRPC_TLS_CERT and GRPC_TLS_KEY, optionally GRPC_CLIENT_CA for mTLS. Clients need matching trust/identity settings. Local plaintext requires explicit GONEX_GRPC_INSECURE=1 for servers and CLIENTS_IDENTITY_INSECURE=1 for clients. Export GONEX_DISABLE_HTTP=1 for a purely gRPC provider. There is no automatic dotenv loading and no generated production secrets.

 Verify service behavior

Library tests exercise real TLS/mTLS. Generated-workspace end-to-end tests use explicit development mode, run independently built provider/consumer binaries, verify an HTTP→gRPC response, terminate the provider and require a bounded dependency-unavailable response. A new client skeleton does not provide that business behavior until its mapping and wiring are completed.

 Run the completed example

Run the completed Identity/Orders example(https://github.com/amkargar/gonex/blob/main/examples/microservices/README.md) for an interactive two-process demo, including tracing, readiness, explicit plaintext development flags and TLS/mTLS configuration. After generating new dependencies, run go mod tidy separately in each service. Export selected HTTP contracts with gonex openapi generate --service orders --http-version v1 --out orders-v1.json when that version is registered.

title: Modules and lifecycle
description: Register explicit Go modules, share business services, and manage resources through startup and graceful shutdown.
text:
Register a module

A module implements Register(app.Registrar) error. Registration declares routes, managed resources and named readiness checks; it should not open listeners or databases. Register related modules together when their declarations must succeed atomically. Registration seals before startup, and retained registrars cannot mutate a running app.

 Keep business logic independent

Keep business services in modules/NAME/service.go. They accept context and domain values and depend on small interfaces owned by their consumer. HTTP schemas/handlers, Protobuf mappers and GORM adapters translate at the boundary. Avoid a shared repository that exposes another service's database.

 Share services across adapters

Generated modules expose an injectable service and NewModuleService; generated registries create one service for all its adapters. Change business logic in handwritten files. Tool-owned registries are hash-checked and must be reconciled explicitly if manually edited.

 Manage resources

Use Registrar.Manage for resources implementing Start(context.Context) error and Close(context.Context) error. Dependencies register before their consumers: database, client pool, then server. Startup failure closes resources already started; shutdown drains HTTP and closes resources in reverse order. Resources can expose an Errors() <-chan error channel for asynchronous failure; App.Run then stops the application and returns an error. Resources must honor their lifecycle contexts.

 Own background work

Start is explicit, Run waits for cancellation/failure, and Shutdown is idempotent. A stopped application cannot restart. Do not start unmanaged goroutines from registration: own their cancellation and join them from a resource's Close method. See operations(/docs/main/operations/) for health checks and shutdown behavior.

title: Operations and readiness
description: Configure readiness, graceful shutdown, request metrics, resource ownership and trace propagation.
text:
Health and readiness

/healthz reports that HTTP is serving. /readyz returns 200 only while the application is running and its managed readiness resources and named checks succeed; otherwise it returns a redacted 503. Registrar.Check(name, func(context.Context) error) registers an application-specific check. Checks share a one-second budget and must honor context. The GORM resource pings its pool; the gRPC server checks its transport lifecycle. Check downstream RPC availability explicitly with Clients.Ready, rather than assuming a constructed client is connected.

 Propagate trace context

observability.HTTP(metrics) is optional Gin middleware installed through config.Config.Middleware. It accepts valid version-00 traceparent headers, preserves the trace ID and creates a new span ID. Invalid/duplicate headers start a fresh trace. observability.Traceparent(ctx) reads the current value. Optional observability/grpc.Client and Server unary interceptors propagate it across services; credentials and arbitrary incoming metadata are not forwarded. Streaming trace propagation and an OTLP exporter are not implemented.

 Collect metrics

observability.NewMetrics() is a managed resource. Counters track completed requests, errors, in-flight work and cumulative elapsed nanoseconds by fixed route/RPC name. Unknown HTTP URLs share an unmatched label; raw URLs, user IDs and secrets are excluded. SnapshotContext copies measurements for a caller-owned exporter. Call SetReadiness(application.Ready) to include dependency readiness; without that callback, readiness represents the metrics resource's lifecycle only. This is an in-process snapshot, without histograms, persistence or a Prometheus server.

 Expose example metrics

The basic example enables tracing/counters and exposes its JSON metrics route only with GONEX_EXPOSE_METRICS=1. Protect that route at your deployment boundary if enabled. There is no exporter endpoint by default in framework applications.

 Drain and stop services

Shutdown first stops accepting HTTP traffic and drains active requests within the shutdown budget, then closes managed resources in reverse order. gRPC uses graceful stop with a forced stop when its context expires. Signal handling belongs to the executable. HTTP deadline middleware cancels request contexts; handlers and dependency calls must honor them. A handler that ignores context cannot be forcibly interrupted safely.

 Verify operational behavior

Run go test ./tests ./grpc for readiness, HTTP drain, asynchronous resource failure, RPC graceful/forced stop, stream deadlines, trace propagation and error-redaction regressions. See the runnable service example(https://github.com/amkargar/gonex/blob/main/examples/microservices/README.md) for HTTP-to-gRPC requests and provider failure.

title: Quick start
description: Run the Gonex basic example, inspect health and users endpoints, and build the CLI from source.
text:
Run the existing example first, then create an application or register a typed endpoint directly. No database is required for the basic HTTP example.


 Requirements

Use Go 1.27.1, the repository baseline, and a populated module cache or network access for dependency downloads. No published framework release is available yet. The CLI defaults generated projects to v0.1.0; use a local checkout override during development.

 Run the basic example

From the repository root:

sh
go run ./examples/basic


In a second terminal:

sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/users/1


Expect "status":"ok" and "id":"1","name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com". The listener defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080. HTTP_ADDRESS overrides it; Ctrl+C drains requests and closes managed resources. The example uses memory unless DATABASE_URL is set.

/readyz reports dependency readiness; /openapi.json exposes the typed API contract. For persistent storage, follow databases and migrations(/docs/main/database/). For optional metrics, see operations(/docs/main/operations/).

 Build the CLI

On macOS/Linux:

sh
go build -o gonex ./cmd/gonex


On Windows:

powershell
go build -o gonex.exe ./cmd/gonex
.\gonex.exe --help


Put the executable on your PATH to use gonex from generated projects. After a release is published, install its exact version with go install github.com/amkargar/gonex/cmd/gonex@VERSION, replacing VERSION with that release tag.

 Create a project

sh
gonex new shop --module example.com/acme/shop
cd shop
gonex create module users
gonex create module reports --transport none


Before resolving dependencies, configure the local override below if the framework version is unpublished. Then:

sh
go mod tidy
gonex check
gonex run


GET /users returns "message":"users". run invokes Go directly; build builds packages; check tests, vets and builds. Child failures preserve their exit codes.

 Use an unpublished checkout

For local development only, point the generated module at your checkout before running go mod tidy. On Windows, replace the example path as needed:

powershell
go mod edit -replace=github.com/amkargar/gonex=D:/Projects/gonex
go mod tidy


On macOS/Linux, use your absolute checkout path, for example go mod edit -replace=github.com/amkargar/gonex=/path/to/gonex. This is an explicit local development override; the generator does not insert machine-specific paths. Remove it with go mod edit -dropreplace=github.com/amkargar/gonex and resolve a published version before deployment.

Microservices also depend on the independent contracts module. Resolve or override that module separately in each service; see the microservices guide(/docs/main/microservices/). Run go mod tidy after generators add dependencies.

 Register a typed endpoint

The following complete program registers one module and one typed route. Save it as main.go in a module that resolves the framework:

go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/amkargar/gonex"
	"github.com/amkargar/gonex/app"
	"github.com/amkargar/gonex/config"
	transport "github.com/amkargar/gonex/http"
)

type greeting struct 
	Message string json:"message"


type helloModule struct

func (helloModule) Register(r app.Registrar) error 
	return transport.Register(r, transport.Endpointtransport.NoBody, greeting
		Method:      "GET",
		Path:        "/hello",
		OperationID: "hello",
		Status:      200,
		Handler: func(context.Context, transport.NoBody) (greeting, error) 
			return greetingMessage: "Hello from goNex", nil
		,
	)


func main() 
	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	a, err := gonex.New(config.Config)
	if err != nil 
		log.Fatal(err)
	
	if err = a.Register(helloModule); err != nil 
		log.Fatal(err)
	
	if err = a.Run(ctx); err != nil 
		log.Fatal(err)
	



GET /hello returns "message":"Hello from goNex" and appears in /openapi.json. In an application, move business behavior into a service and keep transport DTOs and mapping in the adapter. See modules(/docs/main/modules/) and HTTP contracts(/docs/main/http/).

 Add persistence or API versions

gonex create module messages --db adds a local Store interface, GORM adapter/model and an explicit migration with a seeded message. Set DATABASE_URL and optionally DATABASE_DIALECT, then run gonex db migrate before serving. gonex db status prints migration history. There is no automatic .env loading.

For an initially versioned API:

sh
gonex create module catalog --http-version v1
go mod tidy
gonex openapi generate --http-version v1 --out v1.json
gonex openapi validate --file v1.json


This registers catalog under /api/v1 without legacy catalog routes. Compare a future export with a reviewed baseline using gonex openapi validate --file v1.json --against baseline.json. See versioning(/docs/main/versioning/) and upgrades(/docs/main/upgrades/).

 Generator safety

Use --dry-run on generator commands to inspect plans without changing project files. Handwritten source is not overwritten. .gonex.json records template format and hashes for tool-owned registries; edits to those files cause a conflict before writes. Existing destination directories are refused for new projects.

Writes are staged, guarded with an exclusive lock and rolled back on ordinary application errors. Interrupted OS/process failures may require inspecting .gonex.lock; multi-file writes are not crash-atomic. Symlinks, traversal and invalid names are rejected. Names are lowercase Go identifiers; module paths and framework versions follow Go validation.

 Next steps

- CLI reference(/docs/main/cli/): command syntax and flags.
- Modules and lifecycle(/docs/main/modules/): service injection and resource ownership.
- Typed HTTP and OpenAPI(/docs/main/http/): input origins, validation and contracts.
- Optional gRPC(/docs/main/grpc/) and microservices(/docs/main/microservices/): independent service boundaries.
- Operations(/docs/main/operations/) and security(/docs/main/security/): readiness, shutdown and deployment defaults.
- Runnable Identity/Orders example(https://github.com/amkargar/gonex/blob/main/examples/microservices/README.md): a completed HTTP-to-gRPC mapping.

title: Release policy
description: Understand the Gonex development snapshot, release process, verification requirements and current limits.
text:
Current support status

This checkout is not a published release. Local Windows/amd64 verification is recorded in the phase reports. Linux/Windows Go 1.27.1 and latest 1.27 patch are configured CI targets; successful hosted runs are required before claiming that support matrix is verified. Other Go releases and operating systems are unverified. Release builds target Linux, Windows and macOS on amd64/arm64; cross-building alone does not prove runtime support.

 Release checklist

Before a release:

1. Run the test workflow on the release commit: formatting, module verification, tests/vet/build, generated projects, real SQLite, disposable PostgreSQL, Linux race detector, OpenAPI validation/compatibility and benchmark budgets.
2. Run the contracts workflow: pinned official Buf lint/breaking, internal compatibility checks and reproducible official Protobuf generation with a clean generated diff.
3. Review changelog, upgrade instructions, security defaults, examples and all public contract baselines. Baseline updates require review against the previous release, rather than bypassing compatibility checks.
4. Resolve the public repository/module location, choose a semantic tag, and verify generated projects against the resolvable version without local replacements. Publish the independent contracts module under its own module tag when changed.
5. Tag only the reviewed commit. The release workflow reruns reusable test/contracts gates, cross-builds the CLI with an embedded version and uploads checksummed artifacts. It does not publish a GitHub release or push tags.
6. Inspect artifacts and hosted results before separately authorizing publication. Record the actual support matrix and release notes.

 Maintenance and security reports

Only the latest published patch in the active release line is intended to receive fixes; there are no published supported releases yet. Security reports should use a private reporting channel established by the repository owner before publication; do not place credentials or exploit details in public issues. See security configuration(/docs/main/security/).

 Known limits and future scope

Known limits: static service targets, cooperative cancellation, additive migrations without automatic rollback, conservative compatibility checks, no automatic business mapping, no distributed tracing exporter or streaming trace propagation. Brokers, an admin panel and advanced discovery remain future work.

title: Security configuration
description: Review Gonex request limits, authentication boundaries, CORS policy and secure transport configuration.
text:
Authentication and authorization

Authentication is application-owned. security.Authenticate(verifier) delegates credential extraction and verification, requires a nonempty subject and returns a generic 401 on failure. security.Current(ctx) reads the principal. security.Authorize(predicate) returns 403 for a rejected authenticated principal. Install authentication before authorization. Declare matching endpoint error statuses and OpenAPI security schemes; metadata alone does not enforce authentication. No JWT/session scheme is assumed.

 CORS policy

No CORS middleware is enabled automatically. security.CORS accepts explicit HTTP(S) origins, methods and header allowlists, validates configuration and denies unknown origins/preflights. Wildcards are rejected. Credentials are opt-in; preflight caching is limited to 24 hours. CORS does not replace authentication or CSRF defenses for cookie-based applications.

 Request limits and deadlines

Typed bodies default to 1 MiB and reject unknown fields, duplicate keys, trailing JSON, incorrect field case and null nonnullable values. Parameter duplicates and nonfinite floats are rejected. Use pointer DTO fields for optional/presence-sensitive values and pointer nested input objects. Set MaxBodyBytes for an endpoint and http.Deadline for cooperative request deadlines. Server defaults are read 10s, write 30s, idle 60s and shutdown 10s. Configure ingress and application budgets together.

 Transport security

The HTTP listener is plain HTTP intended for a configured TLS ingress or private local deployment. gRPC requires TLS 1.2 or newer; loading helpers support CA verification and mTLS. Plaintext requires explicit DevelopmentInsecure; clients reject skipped certificate verification. No automatic RPC retries are enabled. Managed clients apply a five-second default unary/stream deadline, bounded by an earlier caller deadline.

 Error and secret redaction

Internal errors, panic payloads, readiness failures and database startup credentials are redacted at framework boundaries. Recovery does not dump request headers or panic values. Application logs, SQL logging, explicit public error messages and caller-supplied interceptors remain the application's responsibility. Trace identifiers are correlation data, never authentication credentials.

 Documentation and metrics exposure

OpenAPI is enabled by default: set DisableOpenAPI when it should not be public. /docs is opt-in and loads no external assets. Trusted proxies are disabled unless configured outside the framework's router. Metrics exposure is opt-in in the example. Load secrets from deployment configuration; do not commit credentials.

title: Compatibility and upgrades
description: Pin Gonex versions and review HTTP, Protobuf and generated-code compatibility before upgrading.
text:
Module version policy

goNex uses semantic module versions. Until v1, minor versions may change APIs and templates; patch versions should preserve behavior except documented bug/security fixes. Review the changelog, pin the framework version and upgrade in a branch. No automatic migration of handwritten code is provided.

 Upgrade checklist

1. Update the framework requirement and run go mod tidy independently in each service.
2. Review DTO validation, lifecycle behavior and generated registries before regenerating. .gonex.json format 1 records hashes; generators refuse changed owned files and incompatible layouts. Resolve conflicts explicitly rather than deleting metadata.
3. Run tests, vet, build, migration checks and contract generation/checks. Database migrations are ordered immutable files: append a migration instead of editing applied SQL. Take deployment-specific backups before applying schema changes.
4. Export every supported HTTP version and compare its release baseline. Deploy consumers/providers in a compatible order before retiring old contracts.

 HTTP compatibility

HTTP compatibility includes methods/paths, operation IDs, parameter locations/types/requiredness, body schemas, response status/schema and security requirements. gonex openapi validate --file current.json --against baseline.json performs a conservative comparison: additions are allowed but changes to existing contracts are rejected, including some harmless descriptive edits. Review such changes explicitly; do not silently replace the baseline. Keep separate baselines for each HTTP major. See versioning(/docs/main/versioning/).

 Protobuf compatibility

Protobuf packages encode the API major (identity.v1). Keep field numbers/types, service/method identities and request/response types compatible. Run both gonex grpc check and Buf breaking against the released descriptor baseline. Removing/repurposing fields or methods requires a new version and a consumer migration. The internal checker is deliberately conservative; Buf is an additional release gate.

 Strict DTO changes

This implementation tightens early-phase behavior: duplicate JSON keys and unsupported validation tags now fail; nested request objects require pointers; custom JSON encodings require explicit transport DTOs. A value body wrapper is already required and should not carry validate:"required"; use a pointer if the body's explicit presence is validated. Deadline failures have a documented 504 response. These changes prevent runtime/schema disagreement; update DTOs rather than weakening exported contracts.

 Template compatibility

Templates do not infer business mappings. Older module layouts require the injectable service factory before automatic gRPC enable. Existing handwritten adapters are retained when versions are added; --policy replace is an explicit legacy-route registration change.

title: HTTP API versions
description: Keep version-specific HTTP adapters and contracts separate while sharing business behavior in Gonex.
text:
Add an HTTP version

sh
gonex module version users --http v1 --policy preserve --dry-run
gonex module version users --http v1
gonex module version users --http v2


 Preserve or replace legacy routes

The default preserve policy retains existing handlers and URLs. Adapter sources are copied into independent http/v1 and http/v2 packages; generated registration calls them with one shared service instance. Handwritten handlers, service/repository/model files and prior version packages are untouched. Reruns fail without overwriting. Resolve an edited generated registry before retrying.

--policy replace explicitly stops registering legacy routes, while retaining their source files. That choice persists when later versions are added. No command deletes v1. Deprecation and retirement are application decisions; announce retirement and remove old registrations only as an explicit breaking change.

 Choose a prefix

Default prefixes are /api/v1, /api/v2. Use --prefix /custom/v1 when generating, or http.WithVersion(registrar,"v1",prefix) when registering manually. Versions are positive major identifiers (v1, v2, ...), never v0 or arbitrary path fragments. Version registration changes the typed contract and runtime path together, adds an operation-ID suffix and refuses collisions.

 Export independent contracts

/openapi.json describes legacy routes. /openapi/v1.json and /openapi/v2.json describe their respective effective paths and independent schemas; each document validates against OpenAPI 3.1. App.OpenAPIVersion("v1") exports a registered document without listening and rejects unknown versions. All public documents are disabled together with DisableOpenAPI. CLI export defaults to the legacy document; select a version with gonex openapi generate --http-version v1 --out v1.json.

 Start with a versioned module

Create an initially versioned module with gonex create module catalog --http-version v1. This profile starts directly with http/v1 and does not register legacy routes. Compare each released document using gonex openapi validate --file current.json --against baseline.json; see compatibility policy(/docs/main/upgrades/).

 Handle custom adapter layouts

Version generation expects the Phase 4 adapter Register signature and generated HTTP registry hook. Custom adapter layouts/signatures may require a manual registration change; conflicts must be resolved before generation. Copying a version does not infer a new business API: edit its schemas and handlers to define the intended compatibility boundary.
